verdict.summary: PagerDuty has two OAuth types: Classic User OAuth works on any customer account as soon as you register it, but it only offers broad read or write access, while the recommended Scoped OAuth must be published (review aimed at 5 business days) and then installed by an admin on each customer account. Registering an app needs a Manager, Global Admin or Account Owner role, and PKCE plus a 30-second authorization code make the flow strict.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: App Registration is a short wizard; Scoped OAuth app tokens via client_credentials work on your own account immediately.

timeToProd.assumes: A Scoped OAuth app with granular scopes such as incidents.read, which PagerDuty recommends; a Classic User OAuth app with read or write works across accounts the same day with no review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: PagerDuty's publish review (aim: 5 business days, plus any change requests), then an admin on each customer account installing the app.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 5-business-day target is PagerDuty's; the 1–2 week range adds a round of feedback and is our estimate.

prerequisites.item: A PagerDuty account (customer or developer account) where you have a Manager, Global Admin or Account Owner base role
prerequisites.why: App Registration is available only to those roles.
Use of PagerDuty Developer Services is governed by it.

prerequisites.item: PKCE support in your OAuth client
prerequisites.why: Scoped OAuth apps must always use PKCE; Classic public clients must too.

prerequisites.item: App documentation and support contact for publishing
prerequisites.why: The Distribution Form asks for listing info, docs, support contact and testing instructions.

scopeTiers.impact: Works across accounts as soon as it's registered. read is read-only and write is read/write on all PagerDuty resources the user can access. Legacy, and a broad trust ask.
Granular per-resource scopes and client_credentials app tokens, but only on the account that registered the app.

After publish approval, an admin on each account installs it via https://app.pagerduty.com/oauth_apps/[app_id], then each user authorizes and gets a user token. App tokens aren't available on other accounts.

steps.title: Sign in with a Manager or Admin role
steps.detail: Log in to your PagerDuty account (or a developer account) and open Integrations → Developer Tools → App Registration.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20 (not signed in); the menu path is from the docs.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Click New App, enter a name and description, and add OAuth 2.0 functionality. Apps are tied to a subdomain and a user and can't be moved, so use a shared service user.

steps.title: Choose Scoped or Classic and pick scopes
steps.detail: Map agent actions to scopes from the API reference (each endpoint lists its required scope). Prefer Scoped OAuth with only the resource scopes you need.

steps.title: Save redirect URLs and credentials
steps.detail: Add your redirect URL(s) on the Configure OAuth 2.0 screen, register, and copy the client ID and client secret.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Field order comes from a third-party setup guide; PagerDuty's register page doesn't list redirect URL rules.

steps.title: Implement the PKCE authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope (including as_account-{us|eu}.{subdomain} for Scoped), state and an S256 code_challenge. Exchange the code at https://identity.pagerduty.com/oauth/token within 30 seconds.

steps.title: Implement refresh
steps.detail: Scoped user tokens: 1-day access, 30-day refresh, 1-year rolling window. Classic: 30-day access, 210-day refresh, 3-year rolling window. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token.

steps.title: Write app docs and testing instructions
steps.detail: Fill PagerDuty's app documentation template, support contact, website links and step-by-step test instructions for reviewers.

steps.title: Submit the Distribution Form
steps.detail: Set App Type to Public and submit the Distribution Form. The app is locked after submission; changes need an email to apps@pagerduty.com.

steps.title: Wait for PagerDuty review
steps.detail: Reviewers test functionality and docs and reply to the account email with approval or feedback.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: 'We aim to review your submission and approve or reply with feedback within 5 business days.'

steps.title: Have customer admins install the app
steps.detail: Each customer account's admin opens https://app.pagerduty.com/oauth_apps/[app_id] to install; installing grants no access by itself, so users then authorize individually.

agentCanDo: Pick least-privilege scopes from the API reference
Write the PKCE authorize, fast code exchange and refresh code
Build the as_account-{region}.{subdomain} scope for each customer
Fill the app documentation template and reviewer test steps
Write admin install instructions for customers
humanMustDo: Sign in with a Manager, Global Admin or Account Owner role
Register the app and copy the client secret
Get each customer admin to install the app

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails even though the code just arrived
blockers.cause: The authorization code is valid for only 30 seconds.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code immediately in the callback; avoid queues or extra redirects before the token call.

blockers.symptom: Connect succeeds but every API call returns 403
blockers.cause: Classic scope requests aren't validated; an invalid or mis-cased scope silently yields only openid.
blockers.fix: Request exactly read or write (case sensitive) for Classic, or the documented resource scopes for Scoped.

blockers.symptom: Scoped OAuth app works on your account but not on a customer's
blockers.cause: Unpublished Scoped OAuth apps work only on the registering account, and published ones need an admin install per account.
blockers.fix: Publish the app, then have each customer admin install it at /oauth_apps/[app_id].

blockers.symptom: client_credentials token request fails for a customer account
blockers.cause: App tokens are issued only for the account that created the app.
blockers.fix: Use per-user authorization code tokens on customer accounts.

blockers.symptom: Token endpoint returns {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Client or client authentication not configured on profile"}
blockers.cause: Unknown client_id or missing/incorrect client authentication.
blockers.fix: Check the client ID and secret from App Registration; Classic public clients omit the secret but must use PKCE.

blockers.symptom: You can't change the app after submitting it for review
blockers.cause: Submitting the Distribution Form locks the app.
blockers.fix: Finish testing first; for changes, email apps@pagerduty.com.

blockers.symptom: Tokens keep working after you delete OAuth functionality
blockers.cause: Deleting OAuth functionality doesn't revoke existing tokens.
blockers.fix: Click Revoke All Tokens first, then delete.

nuances.text: Scoped OAuth requires an as_account-{region}.{subdomain} scope (region us or eu), so you need each customer's subdomain and region before starting the flow.

Token lifetimes: Scoped user tokens last 1 day with 30-day refresh tokens (1-year rolling window); Classic tokens last 30 days with 210-day refresh tokens (3-year rolling window). The Classic example response shows expires_in 864000 (10 days), which conflicts with the stated 30 days.
Apps are tied to a PagerDuty subdomain and a user and can't be moved, so register from a durable service account, not a person who may leave.
Publishing also lists the app in the Add Integrations list in the Service Directory, which helps discovery. For Classic apps it's recommended but optional.
PagerDuty issues a signed ID token showing the account, user and service region; use its aud for data-residency routing between US and EU.
No OIDC discovery document is served at identity.pagerduty.com/.well-known/openid-configuration, so configure endpoints by hand.
